sounds.name: First Polyrhythm
sounds.ref: In the style of the manual’s guided start, “Exploring your Subharmonicon”
sounds.blurb: Four notes from Sequencer 1, stepped by two rhythms at once: two against three.
sounds.how: The manual starts here: VCO 1 alone, Sequencer 1 moving its pitch in a chromatic scale, and one rhythm generator stepping it. A second rhythm on the same sequencer adds its own steps, so the four notes fall in a pattern that only comes round again when the two rhythms meet on a downbeat. The manual sets ±2 octaves and 12-ET; the step values and tempo here are this lesson’s.

steps.title: Tune four steps
steps.why:
Give Sequencer 1 the pitch of VCO 1, and four steps that snap to the twelve notes.
- QUANTIZE 12-ET
- SEQ OCT ±2
- SEQ 1 ASSIGN OSC 1 lit
- SEQ 1 STEP 1 0 · 0 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 2 0.63 · +3 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 3 1.46 · +7 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 4 2.08 · +10 st
- Listen for: nothing yet: the sequencer waits for a rhythm and PLAY.

steps.title: A rhythm, then PLAY
steps.why:
Rhythm 1 steps Sequencer 1 on every second clock, and each step plays the envelopes (EG is on).
- TEMPO 5 · 245 BPM
- RHYTHM 1 ÷2
- RHYTHM 1 SEQ 1 lit
- PLAY lit
- VCA DECAY 5 · 220 ms
- CUTOFF 6 · 1.3 kHz
- VCF EG AMT 2 · +3.2 oct
- VCF DECAY 4 · 100 ms
- Listen for: C, E♭, G, B♭ round and round, each note a soft pluck.

steps.title: Add a second rhythm
steps.why:
Rhythm 2 steps the same sequencer on every third clock. Where the two coincide it steps once.
- RHYTHM 2 ÷3
- RHYTHM 2 SEQ 1 lit
- Listen for: the four notes now limping in a two-against-three pattern that repeats every six clocks.

context.rhythm2.div: In this sound: the second rhythm, which makes the pattern lopsided.
context.seq1.step3: In this sound: the third note of the four.

tweaks.hear: A longer, stranger pattern: two against five.
Half the speed, so the pattern is easy to follow.

sounds.name: Mixtur Chord
sounds.ref: In the style of Oskar Sala’s Mixtur-Trautonium
sounds.blurb: Each key plays a chord of undertones under the note, as Sala’s Mixtur-Trautonium did.
sounds.how: The Subharmonicon’s subs come from Oskar Sala’s Mixtur-Trautonium, which divided each note into lower notes of the undertone series. Here VCO 1 plays the key and its two subs divide it by 3 and by 4: an octave and a fifth down, and two octaves down. Every note brings its chord along, in parallel, so a melody becomes a moving block of organ-like sound.

steps.title: Two undertones
steps.why:
Divide VCO 1 by 3 and by 4, and bring both subs into the mix under it.
- VCO 1 SUB 1 FREQ ÷3
- VCO 1 SUB 2 FREQ ÷4
- VCO 1 LEVEL 5
- VCO 1 SUB 1 LEVEL 5
- VCO 1 SUB 2 LEVEL 4
- Listen for: every key a three-note chord: the note, an octave and a fifth below, two octaves below.

steps.title: Shape it
steps.why:
Darken the ladder filter, let the VCF EG brighten each note’s start, and soften the VCA’s edges.
- CUTOFF 5 · 632 Hz
- RESONANCE 3
- VCF EG AMT 1.5 · +2.4 oct
- VCF ATTACK 3 · 16 ms
- VCF DECAY 6 · 480 ms
- VCA ATTACK 3 · 16 ms
- VCA DECAY 6 · 480 ms
- Listen for: a reedy, organ-like chord that swells a little and rings on after each key.

context.sub11.div: In this sound: the middle note of each chord.
context.sub12.div: In this sound: the chord’s root, two octaves down.
context.vcf.cutoff: In this sound: how bright the chord is.

tweaks.hear: A minor colour: the fifth undertone is a major third’s octave below.
A hollower, clarinet-like chord.

sounds.name: Rhythmicon Ratios
sounds.ref: In the style of Henry Cowell’s Rhythmicon (1931)
sounds.blurb: Rhythms at two, three and four beats, under a chord in the same ratios.
sounds.how: Henry Cowell’s Rhythmicon played rhythms in whole-number ratios, each a note of the matching harmonic, so pitch and pulse were one idea. The Subharmonicon’s rhythm generators are that idea: here three rhythms step Sequencer 1 at /2, /3 and /4 of the tempo, while VCO 1’s subs sound the chord at /3 and /4 of its pitch. The pattern repeats every twelve clocks.

steps.title: A chord in the ratios
steps.why:
Divide VCO 1 by 3 and by 4 and mix all three, on square for a clear, woody tone.
- VCO 1 WAVE Square
- VCO 1 SUB 1 FREQ ÷3
- VCO 1 SUB 2 FREQ ÷4
- VCO 1 LEVEL 4
- VCO 1 SUB 1 LEVEL 5
- VCO 1 SUB 2 LEVEL 5
- Listen for: with a key held, a hollow chord in the ratio 4 : 3 : 1… under the note.

steps.title: Three rhythms on one sequencer
steps.why:
Rhythms 2, 3 and 4 (at /2, /3 and /4 as they come) all step Sequencer 1, and every step plays the envelopes.
- RHYTHM 2 SEQ 1 lit
- RHYTHM 3 SEQ 1 lit
- RHYTHM 4 SEQ 1 lit
- TEMPO 5.5 · 315 BPM
- VCA DECAY 4 · 100 ms
- CUTOFF 6.5 · 1.8 kHz
- VCF EG AMT 2.5 · +4 oct
- VCF DECAY 3 · 49 ms
- PLAY lit
- Listen for: a knocking pulse that bunches and spreads, the same twelve clocks over and over.

steps.title: Let the steps move the pitch
steps.why:
Give Sequencer 1 the pitch of VCO 1, on the twelve equal notes, so each rhythm’s steps land on different notes.
- QUANTIZE 12-ET
- SEQ OCT ±1
- SEQ 1 ASSIGN OSC 1 lit
- SEQ 1 STEP 2 2.08 · +5 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 3 2.92 · +7 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 4 -1.25 · -3 st
- Listen for: the pulse turning into a tune whose shape follows the rhythm.

sounds.name: Poly Rock
sounds.ref: In the style of the manual’s Poly Rock patch
sounds.blurb: Sub chords stepped by both sequencers, with a drum pulse from CLOCK OUT.
sounds.how: The manual’s Poly Rock tunes the four subs to chord shapes and patches CLOCK OUT into the VCA input for “drums”: every clock opens the amplifier a little on its own, a beat under the sequenced chords. The manual’s patch sheet transcribes the cables; its knobs and buttons are drawn, not written, so the settings here are this lesson’s.

sounds.name: Cloud Path
sounds.ref: In the style of the manual’s Cloud Path patch
sounds.blurb: Slow, soft chords from both sequencers, with no cables at all.
sounds.how: The manual’s Cloud Path uses no cables: both sequencers and all four subs, tuned with their levels open, then faded in while it plays; RHYTHM 3 SEQ 1 doubles Sequencer 1’s pace. Long envelopes blur each step into the next. The manual’s patch sheet transcribes the cables; its knobs and buttons are drawn, not written, so the settings here are this lesson’s.

sounds.name: Aquatic Chords
sounds.ref: In the style of the manual’s Aquatic Chords patch
sounds.blurb: Each sequencer plays the other VCO, and the envelopes bend the rhythms.
sounds.how: The manual’s Aquatic Chords crosses the sequencers over, SEQ 1 into VCO 2 and SEQ 2 into VCO 1, patches the two envelopes into Rhythms 1 and 2 so each note changes the next rhythm, and fires the envelopes from SEQ 1 CLK alone. The manual’s patch sheet transcribes the cables; its knobs and buttons are drawn, not written, so the settings here are this lesson’s.

steps.title: Cross the sequencers
steps.why:
Tune the steps, run each sequencer from a rhythm, and patch each one into the other VCO.
- SEQ OCT ±1
- SEQ 1 STEP 2 1.46 · +3.5 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 3 -1.25 · -3 st

steps.title: Envelopes bend the rhythms
steps.why:
Each envelope lowers a rhythm’s divisor while it is high, so a note hurries the next steps.
- RHYTHM 1 ÷5
- RHYTHM 2 ÷6
- VCA DECAY 7 · 1.0 s
- Patch VCA EG OUT to RHYTHM 2 input
- Patch VCF EG OUT to RHYTHM 1 input

sounds.name: Mellow Harmonies

sounds.blurb: Sequencer 1 sets the pulse width and Sequencer 2 moves the filter.
sounds.how: The manual’s Mellow Harmonies patches SEQ 1 into VCO 1 PWM, so each step gives the square a different width, and SEQ 2 into CUTOFF, so the other sequencer plays the filter. The manual’s patch sheet transcribes the cables; its knobs and buttons are drawn, not written, so the settings here are this lesson’s.

sounds.name: Point Zero
sounds.ref: In the style of the manual’s Point Zero patch
sounds.blurb: Each sequencer rewrites its own rhythm, with the clocks playing filter and VCA.
sounds.how: The manual’s Point Zero feeds each sequencer back into a rhythm generator (SEQ 1 into RHYTHM 1, SEQ 2 into RHYTHM 2), so every step changes when the next one comes, and patches SEQ 1 CLK into CUTOFF and SEQ 2 CLK into the VCA. VCF ATTACK sets how long each sweep takes. The manual’s patch sheet transcribes the cables; its knobs and buttons are drawn, not written, so the settings here are this lesson’s.

sounds.name: Three Hands on the Wheel

sounds.how: The manual’s Three Hands on the Wheel needs one cable, VCF EG OUT into RHYTHM 1: each time the envelopes fire, Rhythm 1 speeds up for a moment, so the two lines pull ahead and fall back like three hands steering. sounds.name: Bateria
sounds.ref: In the style of the manual’s Bateria patch
sounds.blurb: A pitched kick from the filter and envelopes, its tuning set by Sequencer 1.
sounds.how: The manual’s Bateria (Portuguese for a drum kit) turns the synth into a kick: SEQ 1 into CUTOFF tunes each hit, SEQ 2 into VCO 1 PWM changes its texture, and VCF DECAY and EG AMT give it its flavour. Short envelopes and a resonant filter swept down do the drumming. The manual’s patch sheet transcribes the cables; its knobs and buttons are drawn, not written, so the settings here are this lesson’s.

sounds.name: Star-Gate
sounds.ref: In the style of the manual’s Star-Gate patch
sounds.blurb: High, glittering sequences whose third rhythm the filter envelope keeps moving.
sounds.how: The manual’s Star-Gate runs high sequences, patches VCA EG OUT into CUTOFF and VCF EG OUT into RHYTHM 3, and asks you to vary Rhythms 2 to 4 on Sequencer 2 and VCA DECAY, and to ride the mixer while it plays. The manual’s patch sheet transcribes the cables; its knobs and buttons are drawn, not written, so the settings here are this lesson’s.

steps.title: High sequences
steps.why:
Both VCOs high, with their subs well down, and both sequencers moving their pitch in wide steps.
- VCO 1 FREQ 4 · G5 · 784 Hz
- VCO 2 FREQ 5 · C6 · 1.0 kHz
- VCO 2 WAVE Square
- VCO 1 LEVEL 3
- VCO 1 SUB 1 LEVEL 3
- VCO 1 SUB 2 LEVEL 2
- VCO 2 LEVEL 3
- VCO 2 SUB 1 LEVEL 3
- VCO 2 SUB 2 LEVEL 2
- VCO 1 SUB 2 FREQ ÷6
- VCO 2 SUB 2 FREQ ÷7
- QUANTIZE 12-ET
- SEQ OCT ±2
- SEQ 1 ASSIGN OSC 1 lit
- SEQ 2 ASSIGN OSC 2 lit
- SEQ 1 STEP 2 1.88 · +9 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 3 -1.25 · -6 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 4 3.13 · +15 st
- SEQ 2 STEP 2 -2.29 · -11 st
- SEQ 2 STEP 3 1.04 · +5 st
- SEQ 2 STEP 4 2.71 · +13 st
- Listen for: with a key held, a high, glassy cluster.

steps.title: Rhythms that wander
steps.why:
Rhythm 1 on Sequencer 1, Rhythms 2 to 4 on Sequencer 2, and the envelopes patched back into the filter and Rhythm 3.
- RHYTHM 1 SEQ 1 lit
- RHYTHM 2 SEQ 2 lit
- RHYTHM 3 ÷9
- RHYTHM 3 SEQ 2 lit
- RHYTHM 4 ÷5
- RHYTHM 4 SEQ 2 lit
- TEMPO 5.5 · 315 BPM
- CUTOFF 4 · 317 Hz
- RESONANCE 3
- VCF EG AMT 2 · +3.2 oct
- VCF DECAY 4 · 100 ms
- VCA DECAY 4 · 100 ms
- PLAY lit
- Patch VCA EG OUT to CUTOFF input
- Patch VCF EG OUT to RHYTHM 3 input
- Listen for: a busy, sparkling pattern that keeps changing its rhythm.

sounds.name: Just Fifths Drone
sounds.ref: In the style of La Monte Young’s just-intonation drones
sounds.blurb: A held drone of fifths and undertones that switches from beating to still with QUANTIZE.
sounds.how: Drone music tuned in just intonation, as La Monte Young’s is, keeps its intervals in pure whole-number ratios, so the notes lock together instead of beating. The Subharmonicon’s subs are whole-number ratios already; QUANTIZE’s 12-JI tunes VCO 2’s fifth to an exact 3 : 2 as well. EG held holds both envelopes open: a drone with no key at all.

steps.title: Hold the envelopes open
steps.why:
EG held keeps both envelopes at full, so the synth sounds with nothing playing.
- EG Held
- CUTOFF 5 · 632 Hz
- RESONANCE 2
- Listen for: VCO 1 sounding steadily on its own.

steps.title: Fifths and undertones
steps.why:
VCO 2 a fifth over VCO 1, on the twelve equal notes first, with subs under both.
- QUANTIZE 12-ET
- VCO 2 FREQ 1.46 · G4 · 392 Hz
- VCO 1 LEVEL 3
- VCO 1 SUB 1 LEVEL 3
- VCO 2 LEVEL 3
- VCO 2 SUB 1 LEVEL 3
- VCO 2 SUB 1 FREQ ÷3
- Listen for: a slow wobble in the chord: the equal-tempered fifth beating against the subs.

steps.title: Just intonation
steps.why:
Switch QUANTIZE to 12-JI: VCO 2’s fifth becomes an exact 3 : 2.
- QUANTIZE 12-JI
- Listen for: the wobble stopping: the drone locks into one still, glowing chord.

sounds.name: Berlin Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of Berlin School sequencer music
sounds.blurb: A rolling sequenced bass, its weight from subs two octaves down.
sounds.how: Berlin School music of the 1970s built long pieces on rolling, repeating sequencer bass lines through a resonant filter. Here Sequencer 1 plays a four-note line on C major, stepped on every clock, and VCO 1’s subs at /2 and /4 give it its depth; the VCF EG plucks every note.

steps.title: Deep sources
steps.why:
VCO 1 with its subs an octave and two octaves down, the subs louder than the VCO.
- VCO 1 SUB 1 FREQ ÷2
- VCO 1 SUB 2 FREQ ÷4
- VCO 1 LEVEL 3
- VCO 1 SUB 1 LEVEL 5
- VCO 1 SUB 2 LEVEL 5
- Listen for: with a key held, a heavy, low tone.

steps.title: Pluck it
steps.why:
A low, resonant cutoff opened briefly by the VCF EG on every note.
- CUTOFF 3 · 159 Hz
- RESONANCE 5
- VCF EG AMT 3 · +4.8 oct
- VCF DECAY 3.5 · 72 ms
- VCA DECAY 4.5 · 150 ms
- Listen for: a squelchy, plucked bass.

steps.title: The sequence
steps.why:
Sequencer 1 moves VCO 1 on C major, one step a clock.
- QUANTIZE 8-ET
- SEQ OCT ±1
- SEQ 1 ASSIGN OSC 1 lit
- SEQ 1 STEP 2 2.92 · +7 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 3 1.46 · +3.5 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 4 4.17 · +10 st
- RHYTHM 1 SEQ 1 lit
- TEMPO 5 · 245 BPM
- PLAY lit
- Listen for: a driving four-note bass line, round and round.

sounds.name: Three Against Four
sounds.ref: In the style of minimalist pattern music (Steve Reich, Terry Riley)
sounds.blurb: Two short melodies, one stepping every third clock and one every fourth, slowly shifting against each other.
sounds.how: Minimalist composers such as Steve Reich and Terry Riley built pieces from short repeating patterns heard against each other, so new figures emerge from the overlap. Here Sequencer 1 steps every three clocks and Sequencer 2 every four: their four-note melodies line up again only every forty-eight clocks.

steps.title: Two voices
steps.why:
VCO 2 an octave over VCO 1, on square, with both in the mix.
- VCO 2 FREQ 2.5 · C5 · 523 Hz
- VCO 2 WAVE Square
- VCO 1 LEVEL 4
- VCO 2 LEVEL 3
- QUANTIZE 8-ET
- CUTOFF 5.5 · 893 Hz
- VCF EG AMT 2 · +3.2 oct
- VCF DECAY 3.5 · 72 ms
- VCA DECAY 4.5 · 150 ms
- Listen for: with a key held, two notes an octave apart, one buzzy, one hollow.

steps.title: Two melodies, two rhythms
steps.why:
Each sequencer moves its VCO; Rhythm 3 (/3) steps Sequencer 1 and Rhythm 4 (/4) Sequencer 2.
- SEQ OCT ±1
- SEQ 1 ASSIGN OSC 1 lit
- SEQ 2 ASSIGN OSC 2 lit
- SEQ 1 STEP 2 1.25 · +3 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 3 2.08 · +5 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 4 0.83 · +2 st
- SEQ 2 STEP 2 -0.83 · -2 st
- SEQ 2 STEP 3 0.42 · +1 st
- SEQ 2 STEP 4 1.67 · +4 st
- RHYTHM 3 SEQ 1 lit
- RHYTHM 4 SEQ 2 lit
- TEMPO 6 · 404 BPM
- PLAY lit
- Listen for: two interlocking figures whose combination keeps changing.

tweaks.hear: Three against five: the cycle stretches to sixty clocks.

sounds.name: Undertone Arpeggio
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s kosmische Musik
sounds.blurb: Sequencer 1 moves the subs’ divisors, not the pitch: an arpeggio down the undertone series.
sounds.how: The ASSIGN buttons can send a sequencer to the subs’ divisors instead of the VCO’s pitch. Then each step picks a different undertone under a VCO that never moves, so the arpeggio always stays inside its subharmonic chord: an otherworldly, kosmische sound with nothing to tune. Here VCO 1 is silent and only its subs play.

steps.title: Only the subs
steps.why:
VCO 1 out of the mix, both its subs in, VCO 1 high so the subs land in the middle.
- VCO 1 FREQ 3 · D5 · 601 Hz
- VCO 1 LEVEL 0
- VCO 1 SUB 1 LEVEL 5
- VCO 1 SUB 2 LEVEL 4
- VCO 1 SUB 1 FREQ ÷6
- VCO 1 SUB 2 FREQ ÷8
- CUTOFF 6 · 1.3 kHz
- RESONANCE 4
- VCF EG AMT 2.5 · +4 oct
- VCF DECAY 4 · 100 ms
- VCA DECAY 5 · 220 ms
- Listen for: with a key held, two low notes of VCO 1’s undertone series.

steps.title: Step the divisors
steps.why:
Sequencer 1 moves both subs’ divisors; a step turned right lowers them, so the sub climbs.
- SEQ OCT ±1
- SEQ 1 ASSIGN SUB 1 lit
- SEQ 1 ASSIGN SUB 2 lit
- SEQ 1 STEP 2 1.7 · +4.1 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 3 3.4 · +8.2 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 4 -1.7 · -4.1 st
- RHYTHM 1 SEQ 1 lit
- RHYTHM 3 SEQ 1 lit
- TEMPO 5.5 · 315 BPM
- PLAY lit
- Listen for: an arpeggio jumping between undertones, always in tune with itself.

sounds.name: Birds
sounds.ref: In the style of Oskar Sala’s bird sounds for The Birds (1963)
sounds.blurb: Screeching, chattering cries from fast high steps and short envelopes.
sounds.how: Oskar Sala made the bird cries in Hitchcock’s The Birds on his Mixtur-Trautonium. A rough idea of them comes from fast, high, unquantised steps on both VCOs, short envelopes and a resonant filter, with two rhythms per sequencer so the chatter never settles into a beat.

steps.title: High and harsh
steps.why:
Both VCOs high on sawtooth, with one sub each, and the filter resonant.
- VCO 1 FREQ 5.5 · D6 · 1.2 kHz
- VCO 2 FREQ 6.2 · F♯6 · 1.5 kHz
- VCO 1 LEVEL 4
- VCO 1 SUB 1 LEVEL 3
- VCO 2 LEVEL 4
- VCO 2 SUB 1 LEVEL 3
- CUTOFF 6 · 1.3 kHz
- RESONANCE 6
- VCF EG AMT 3 · +4.8 oct
- VCF DECAY 2.5 · 33 ms
- VCA DECAY 3 · 49 ms
- Listen for: with a key, a piercing, shrill cry.

steps.title: Chatter
steps.why:

- SEQ OCT ±2

- SEQ 2 ASSIGN OSC 2 lit
- SEQ 1 STEP 1 1.3 · +6.2 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 2 -2.2 · -10.6 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 3 3.1 · +14.9 st
- SEQ 1 STEP 4 -0.7 · -3.4 st
- SEQ 2 STEP 1 -1.6 · -7.7 st
- SEQ 2 STEP 2 2.6 · +12.5 st
- SEQ 2 STEP 3 -3.3 · -15.8 st
- SEQ 2 STEP 4 0.9 · +4.3 st
- RHYTHM 1 SEQ 1 lit
- RHYTHM 3 SEQ 1 lit
- RHYTHM 2 SEQ 2 lit
- RHYTHM 4 ÷5
- RHYTHM 4 SEQ 2 lit
- TEMPO 6.5 · 519 BPM
